title: libpod: unmount the rootfs overlay when mountStorage fails
body:
Fixes #30256

`mountStorage` mounts the `--rootfs :O` overlay, then looks up the container's user and prepares `/etc`, the timezone and volumes. Each error return after the mount left the overlay mounted. `c.state.Mounted` is only set after `mountStorage` succeeds, so `cleanupStorage` skips the unmount, and the overlay outlives the failed start.

This defers `overlay.Unmount(contentDir)` on error right after the overlay is mounted. The SHM and idmapped-rootfs mounts earlier in the function already work this way. If the native `mount.Mount` itself fails, `overlay.Unmount` ignores the merge dir not being a mount point.

The new system test in `030-run.bats` runs `--user nosuchuser --rootfs $rootfs:O` and checks that `<cid>/rootfs/merge` is no longer in the mount table. It reads the table via `podman unshare` when rootless and directly when rootful, and is skipped for remote.

Tested locally, on a v5.8.6 build with this patch (it applies unchanged to `main`, where `go vet ./libpod/` passes):

- The new test passes rootless and rootful with this change. It fails on 5.4.2 without it, because the overlay is still mounted.
- The existing `--rootfs` tests in `030-run.bats` still pass: `check workdir` and `no entrypoint`. `idmapped mounts` was skipped (no subordinate IDs configured).

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a bug where a container using an overlay rootfs (`--rootfs <dir>:O`) that failed to start, for example because its user could not be found, left the rootfs overlay mounted until the container was removed.
```
